key_insight: Scaling Representation Autoencoder (RAE) decoders on a frozen high‑dimensional semantic encoder (SigLIP‑2) and training on combined web, synthetic, and text‑rendered data enables diffusion transformer text‑to‑image models to improve general fidelity and text alignment — but success depends on careful data composition and text‑conditioning.
problem_solved: How to scale RAE‑based diffusion modeling from ImageNet to large‑scale, freeform text‑to‑image generation while preserving image fidelity and accurate text alignment across diverse web-scale data.
method: Freeze a high‑dimensional semantic encoder (SigLIP‑2) and scale the RAE decoder capacity to operate in the encoder's latent space.
Train on a mixed corpus (web images, synthetic renders, and explicit text‑rendered examples) to improve generalization and textual alignment.
Model diffusion with transformer architectures in the representation latent space and apply text‑conditioning strategies (e.g., cross‑attention / classifier‑free guidance) to steer generation.
impact: Provides a practical pathway to scale T2I diffusion models more efficiently by working in semantic latent spaces, improving image fidelity and controllability while reducing some compute and data inefficiencies of pixel‑space training. It highlights the importance of dataset curation and conditioning for reliable text alignment at scale.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: SigLIP‑2 encoder (frozen) → scaled RAE decoder → diffusion transformer with text conditioning (show latent space flow).
Dataset composition pie/chart: proportion of web images vs synthetic vs text‑rendered data and their effect on text alignment.
Before/after image grid: ImageNet‑scale RAE baseline vs scaled RAE decoder outputs showing fidelity and text‑prompt adherence.
Ablation bar chart: impact of decoder scale and presence/absence of text‑rendered data on fidelity and caption alignment metrics.
paper_title: Scaling Text-to-Image Diffusion Transformers with Representation Autoencoders
paper_authors: Shengbang Tong, Boyang Zheng, Ziteng Wang, Bingda Tang, Nanye Ma
